Let’s break down the SVG path data:

`M 12.98,31.92 L 92.45,24.58` — Move to point (12.98,31.92), then draw a line to (92.45,24.58).  
`M 92.45,24.58 L 59.03,76.23 L 12.98,31.92` — Move again to (92.45,24.58) (same point), then draw a line to (59.03,76.23), then a line to (12.98,31.92) (closing back to the first point).

So the path consists of:  
1. A line segment from (12.98,31.92) to (92.45,24.58)  
2. A triangle with vertices (92.45,24.58), (59.03,76.23), and (12.98,31.92) — because the last segment returns to the first point of the triangle.

But note: the first segment is drawn separately, then the triangle is drawn separately (starting again at 92.45,24.58).  
However, the triangle already includes two of the points from the first segment, so the entire figure is just a triangle — the first line is one side of the triangle, and the rest of the path traces the other two sides.

Thus, the entire path is a triangle.

Final answer: (J)
